dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Lorraine. Go ahead.
Yeah, hi, good morning. I know it's Saturday and City Hall's closed, so I'm calling the storm line like the recording said. That's the right number, yeah?
That's right, this line is open for storm and drain problems when the main offices are closed. What's going on?
Storm drain on my corner is full to the top. Not draining at all. We had that rain come in Friday and it wrapped up today, and the water's just sitting there on top of the grate like a bathtub.
Okay, so the drain is full to the brim and the water is not going down. Can I get the address, or the nearest corner?
394 Admiral Kalbfus Road. Up the North End. The drain's right at the corner by my place.
394 Admiral Kalbfus Road. Got it. Is the water getting into your property, or is it mostly in the street?
Mostly the street right now. It's creeping up toward the edge of the driveway, but nothing inside. I just don't want to wait and see, you know? It's been like this since last night.
Understood. Is there anything on top of the grate, leaves, trash, anything like that?

Little bit of leaves, sure, but it's not the leaves. I went out with a rake and cleared the top. Still nothing. Whatever's down there is packed. So I'm asking if somebody can come out and clean it. Get it cleaned out.
Yes, I'll put in a request to have the drain cleaned. I'll note that the grate was cleared by hand and it's still not draining, so it's something further down.
Right. And there's one more thing. There's a manhole cover near it, maybe ten feet over, and it looks off. Like it's sitting an inch higher on one side. Wicked strange. I didn't touch it.
Good, please don't touch it. Is it sitting crooked, or is one edge raised up out of the frame?
One edge is up. About an inch, I'd say. Cars are going over it and it kind of clunks. Probably the water pushing on it, I don't know.
Okay. I'll add that to the same ticket so the crew looks at both. Raised manhole cover, about an inch on one edge, roughly ten feet from the drain. Did I get that right?
That's it. Ten feet, give or take, toward the stop sign.
Toward the stop sign, good. Can I confirm a callback number in case someone needs to reach you?
Sure. It's 401-555-0190. That's the landline, so if I'm out back, let it ring.
401-555-0190. I have that. Now, crews are going to be stretched after a storm like this one, so it may not be today. Is it a safety issue for traffic right now, or just standing water?
Just standing water for now. Cars slow down and go around. But if it freezes tonight, that's another story. It's supposed to dip.

That's worth noting. I'll mark it that water may freeze on the roadway overnight. I'd expect somebody out sometime over the weekend or early in the week, depending on how many calls are ahead of yours.

Okay. Fine. I figured it wouldn't be this minute. Sorry if I sound short. I've got my little guy in the other room and he just learned the word no. Everything is no. You ask him if he wants lunch, no. You ask him if he wants a cookie, no. Then he cries because there's no cookie.
Ha, that's a stage. It does pass eventually.
That's what they tell me. Anyway, the drain. Can you read me back what you've got so I know it's in right?

Sure. 394 Admiral Kalbfus Road, North End, corner storm drain full and not draining after the rain, grate already cleared by hand. Request to clean it out. Also a manhole cover nearby, raised about an inch on one side, toward the stop sign. Possible freezing overnight. Callback 401-555-0190.
Yep, that's all of it. Thanks. I appreciate you picking up on a Saturday.
Of course. If the water starts coming toward the house, call this line back right away and tell them it's an update to the ticket.
Will do. Take care.
You too, Mr. Mancini. Bye now.
